- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.0) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects downward — avoid sharp drops; allow slight lagged rebound.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast rise to 5–7% above prior peak.  
- When sentiment is flat (0.0) and history shows mean-reversion patterns, model often fails to recognize trend reversal — adjust forecast to align with recent 5–7 day average.  
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in first 5–7 days, model is lagging — apply early correction by +2–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- In high-sentiment periods (e.g., 0.27), model often underestimates upside — increase forecast by 1–2% above historical mean for next 3–5 days.  
- If forecast is flat and true outcome shows volatility, model is ignoring sentiment — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment direction, even if price is trending sideways.
